packages.label: תּוֹרָה וְכַלָּה — שִׁדּוּכֵי הַדַּעַת
packages.label_en: Torah and the Bride — The Matchmaking of Da'at
packages.reason: Torah and kallah (bride) share the same essential nature: both are unions of two opposites. Torah contains two types of letters (two opposing dimensions), and a kallah is the product of a shidduch uniting two opposites. The Sages' word-play — read 'betrothed' (me'orasah) rather than 'inheritance' (morasha) — makes the equation explicit and textually grounded. Both concepts also participate in the central act of this Torah: the tzaddik who says Torah is acting as matchmaker, because Torah-as-bride is the object of the shidduch.
